correspondence.component_scope: Selected glacial opening and actual headward route
correspondence.finding: The eastern opening lies on the Gran Cachapoal glacier tongue. Independent satellite pixels show the modeled route running down the ice and debris-covered valley tongue, bending southwest around its southern terminal lobe, then west into the proglacial Cachapoal valley. The neighboring small marginal lake and northern tributary valley are not traversed. Soza and Falaschi locate Gran Cachapoal in this headwater setting, and the independent 2013 EGU abstract describes the Cachapoal glacier descending from Picos del Barroso with a bifurcated terminal tongue. The line is a generalized glacier/drainage axis, not proof of an open surface river throughout the ice-covered reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Cachapoal westward valley and mountain junctions
correspondence.finding: From the proglacial valley the selected course continues west along upper Cachapoal, receiving the distinct Los Baños and Don Manuel-side tributary surroundings from the north. The source shows the separate Cauquencito-side approach to the upper valley and the separate Las Leñas entry from the southeast. The selection remains on the Cachapoal trunk past the Las Leñas, Cortaderal and Los Cipreses joining settings; none of those longer tributary valleys is the selected opening. The river rendering does not depict a river through the glacier, which is supplied by independent image and descriptive coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: Pangal and Coya junctions to the central valley
correspondence.finding: The same feature turns northwest along Cachapoal, passes the separate eastern Pangal contribution and the northern Coya joining setting, then turns southwest and west through the Claro de Cauquenes joining corridor. Its recognizable sequence of bends and tributary mouths continues toward the Rancagua central-valley setting. The northern Pangal and Coya courses and southern Claro approach are neighboring contributors, not selected continuations.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle and lower Cachapoal to La Junta
correspondence.finding: The river source establishes the full westward, southwestward and northwestward Cachapoal corridor through the central valley, with La Cadena and Idahue-side northern contributions and the distinct Río Claro de Rengo and Zamorano-side contributions to the south. The large southern bend is on Cachapoal; the route then turns northwest toward the reservoir head. This feature ends at the Cachapoal–Tinguiririca/La Junta reservoir-inflow setting. The modeled break is not asserted as the exact legal or historical name boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Complete short southern tributary feature
correspondence.finding: The entire small feature occupies the western braided/backwater part of the terminal Tinguiririca approach immediately below the neighboring Las Cadenas joining surroundings and connects northward to the selected Cachapoal–Rapel node. The waterbody rendering places this little arm in the combined river-mouth/reservoir-head setting. It does not represent the full Tinguiririca or Las Cadenas course and has no independently established local branch name. Its connection is visible and complete; exact braid naming and waterline changes are not treated as a material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Rapel reservoir passage and outlet
correspondence.finding: The downstream mainstem feature starts in the La Junta inflow setting, follows the long southern Rapel reservoir axis northward, then bends northwest through the western narrowing to the reservoir outlet and Río Rapel. The labeled waterbody source establishes the entire lake-interior connection that is absent from the river-only rendering. The broad eastern Alhué-side reservoir arm is not selected. This is a generalized traversal of an artificial reservoir, not an independently named open river for every point of the lake interior.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Rapel and coastal receiving setting
correspondence.finding: Below the reservoir outlet the selected course follows the labeled Rapel northwest and west past the Litueche/Quelentaro, Comeche and Rucatalca-side tributary surroundings into the broad La Boca estuarine reach. Independent satellite pixels establish the coastal estuary and ocean connection, while SERNATUR independently identifies La Boca at the Rapel mouth. The selected terminal is seaward of the mapped estuary, in the adjacent Pacific receiving setting. The final straight segment generalizes across the mouth/spit surroundings and is not a claim that a surveyed river channel cuts that exact straight line across the peninsula. The estuary and ocean connection are established without asserting a present-day mouth position or exact channel centerline.

correspondence.component_scope: Whole selected representative system
correspondence.finding: Together the selected glacial opening and Cachapoal trunk, terminal Tinguiririca-side arm, Rapel reservoir and lower Rapel continuation form the connected Rapel system. Río Rapel is supported as the representative identity. This does not propagate that name over Gran Cachapoal glacier, Río Cachapoal, Río Tinguiririca or the reservoir. The model length is not an official river-length claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern mountain hook and Cattle Camp Wash approach
correspondence.finding: The selected initial westward hook follows the mapped mountain drainage east of southern Steptoe Valley. It rounds the southern valley head and turns north into the wash corridor east of the South Egan Range. Cattle Camp Wash is directly labeled farther north on this valley-floor drainage.
correspondence.limits: The initial mountain reach is not given the wash label by proximity alone; no official source vertex or complete uniform upper hydronym is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern valley floor and Steptoe Creek vicinity
correspondence.finding: The selected northbound route continues in the broad axial wash country past the Willow Creek joining surroundings, the southern wetland/pond setting and the Steptoe Creek crossing east of Ely. The mountain branch of Steptoe Creek approaches from the east; the model instead selects the much longer southern valley-floor approach.
correspondence.limits: The model mainstem role is not treated as a source-name hierarchy. No claim that the whole southern wash is Steptoe Creek.

correspondence.component_scope: Ely-to-McGill drainage, Tailings Creek and Bassett Lake
correspondence.finding: North of Ely the selected route remains on the valley floor west of the Duck Creek Range. It approaches the Tailings Creek-labeled corridor along the western side of the large impounded-water setting, passes the Steptoe Slough/Bassett Lake surroundings, and continues into the north-trending lower Duck Creek wetland corridor.
correspondence.limits: No exact impoundment shoreline or distributary assignment is inferred from small-scale offsets. The nearby mountain Duck Creek approach is distinct from the selected southern approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Duck Creek through the Cherry Creek road setting
correspondence.finding: The full long middle section follows the distinctly mapped lower Duck Creek corridor, its wetland and multiple-channel stretches, and the west-of-highway approach through the Cherry Creek road setting. Rabbit Creek, Fitzhugh Creek and the eastern Spring Valley Creek remain separately mapped context.
correspondence.limits: A recognizable generalized corridor does not imply continuously flowing water or a uniform channel through every wetland.

correspondence.component_scope: Goshute Lake approach and selected lake-interior passage
correspondence.finding: North of the Cherry Creek road setting the mapped Duck Creek becomes discontinuous before the large Goshute Lake playa/wetland complex. The selected line continues into and through that complex, then leaves its northern side toward the McDermid Creek surroundings.
correspondence.limits: The lake setting is established, but the source does not establish this as a single northbound through-channel or lake outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Currie-area cross-connection
correspondence.finding: Detailed original cartography places McDermid Creek south of the Currie surroundings and Nelson Creek with its Phalen Creek junction farther north. The selected route joins these settings through an interval for which the map does not show a complete corresponding aquatic connector.
correspondence.limits: The actual connection remains material pending. Nearby mapped ditches or parallel railway alignments cannot be substituted for the selected natural-waterway correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Nelson Creek northeast corridor
correspondence.finding: After the Currie transition, the selected route corresponds to the mapped Nelson Creek valley and its northeastward course between Spruce Mountain and the Dolly Varden Mountains. Phalen Creek joins from the west, and Indian Creek approaches farther north from Spruce Mountain.
correspondence.limits: Nelson Creek is supported for this bounded corridor, not as an alias for the entire selected feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Long final plain and Flowery Lake vicinity
correspondence.finding: The map carries Nelson Creek into the southern Goshute Valley plain, where its plotted channel ends. The selected route continues much farther north across the broad plain, east of the mountains, toward and beyond the Flowery Lake label. Neither the original overview nor the enlarged terminal detail shows a matching complete channel or waterbody passage for this extension.
correspondence.limits: The final receiving feature and actual flow-path correspondence are unresolved. The name Flowery Lake is nearby geographic context, not a demonstrated selected lake passage or terminal identity.

correspondence.component_scope: Independent hydrologic context
correspondence.finding: The 2009 Corps account treats Steptoe and Goshute as closed basins. It describes lower Duck Creek as becoming ephemeral and dissipating near the Goshute Lake playa, while allowing possible shallow surface connection. Nelson and Phalen are separately identified ephemeral Goshute Valley drainages.
correspondence.limits: Historical physical context only; no present-day jurisdictional conclusion, current flow condition or exact selected-line connection is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: State basin disambiguation
correspondence.finding: The Nevada listing separately identifies Steptoe Valley as basin 179 and Goshute Valley as basin 187. Spring Valley is a different listed basin, 184.
correspondence.limits: Administrative basin identities do not name the selected line or establish a surface-water connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Initial southern Monitor alluvial tract
correspondence.finding: The opening lies in the low alluvial ground between the valley margins north of the Belmont surroundings. Finer national cartography shows a nearby eastern drainage labeled Wackles Creek and the Meadow/Barley drainage farther north, but does not establish the actual selected opening as a connected tributary of Meadow Creek. Wackles Creek is not assigned merely because it is nearby.

correspondence.component_scope: Meadow Creek and Pine Creek lowlands
correspondence.finding: Original national labels distinguish Meadow Creek, its wetland-lined valley reach, Pine Creek entering from the Toquima side and continuing north on the valley floor, and separate Corcoran, Barley, Mosquito and Morgan creeks. The selected southern lowland corresponds broadly to the Meadow/Pine corridor after its unresolved opening. Their mountain headwaters are outside the selected route; neither name is extended over the entire modeled feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Dry Lake passage
correspondence.finding: The modeled line crosses the explicitly labeled Dry Lake playa in southern Monitor Valley. Wadsworth Creek enters from the east and is not the selected long southern feeder. The 1964 field report separately records this southern Monitor playa as dry in mid-April and flooded after early-May storm and snowmelt. The Dry Lake interior is treated as a generalized playa passage, not a named permanent river channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Inter-Monitor connection
correspondence.finding: North of Dry Lake the original detail shows Box Spring marsh, the narrow lowland beside bedrock, Crane Creek ending in that setting, and the separate northward spring/wetland corridor near Dianas Punch Bowl. The selected route links these settings, but the inspected maps do not establish the whole link as one surface-water connector. The 1964 text explicitly qualifies infrequent drainage from southern to northern Monitor Valley through the bedrock gap as probable. Groundwater underflow and regional valley membership are not substituted for proof of that surface link.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern Monitor Valley and Stoneberger Creek
correspondence.finding: Beyond the southern connection, the long northern Monitor corridor is repeatedly labeled Stoneberger Creek. Its named mountain branch enters from the west, while Willow Creek and other eastern tributaries are distinct. The selected line follows the lowland Stoneberger corridor northward, curves northeast around the northern Monitor margin and crosses toward Bean Flat and southern Kobeh Valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Kobeh Valley
correspondence.finding: The west-to-east selected corridor corresponds to Stoneberger Creek across the southern valley, joining the Coils/Roberts and Slough Creek setting. The separate Antelope Wash approaches from the south. County prose describes Stoneberger and Slough as dry washes and its original floodplain map follows the same eastward corridor; dry or episodic flow alone is not treated as a correspondence failure.

correspondence.component_scope: Slough Creek and Devils Gate
correspondence.finding: The selection follows Slough Creek south of Lone Mountain through the constrained Devils Gate outlet and turns northeast into Diamond Valley. The county plan documents episodic surface flow through this outlet, while the 1964 reconnaissance reports actual Slough Creek flow at Devils Gate during its field work. This is established surface-water outlet correspondence, independent of groundwater underflow.

correspondence.component_scope: Diamond Valley eastern floodway
correspondence.finding: The county plan distinguishes a floodway from Devils Gate to the valley axis and two downstream branches, one trending toward the western side and the other following the eastern valley. Figure7-9 and the original national relief/channel setting locate the selection along the eastern floodway, toward the southeast margin of the northern playa. The western axial branch and separate Garden Pass, Simpson and Pedrioli drainages are not substituted for the selected branch. The county floodplain correspondence does not assert an uninterrupted perennial or currently active channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Terminal northern Diamond Valley playa
correspondence.finding: The selection enters and ends within the large northern Diamond Valley playa south of Garcia Flat. Original map pixels distinguish the dry-lake floor, marginal marshes and small surrounding basins; the county map identifies the same large terminal floodplain. The modeled interior continuation is a generalized playa representation, not evidence of a river called Slough Creek crossing its whole floor, a route to Humboldt River, or an exact natural mouth vertex. Its terminal-playa setting is established and is not itself the reason for material-pending.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward Pedra–Jacutinga drainage
correspondence.finding: The Fronteira dos Vales original locates the selected opening in the Córrego da Pedra corridor and its southwestward continuation into Córrego Jacutinga. The mapped connected course proceeds south through the Alcobaça/Andaraí surroundings into a reach labeled Rio Itanhém. The separately drawn eastern Córrego Alcobaça through Monte Castelo and the western Encerado approach are not substituted for the selected headward branch. Exact creek-name transition points and an official spring location are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Itanhém west and south of Machacalis
correspondence.finding: The Machacalis original carries the selected southbound course along the western side of the municipality and around its southeastward turn, with Itanhém and Alcobaça labels on the main river. The Rio do Norte approaching from Machacalis and the Água Preta drainage are separate incoming waterways. The modeled route continues along the southern main channel through their junction setting rather than turning north into that tributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Umburatiba junction and Bahia entry
correspondence.finding: The Umburatiba sheet directly labels the selected western-to-southeastern trunk Rio Alcobaça ou Itanhém and shows its junction near Umburatiba with Rio Umburanas from the north. The Itanhém and Medeiros Neto originals overlap this area and continue the trunk past the Damazinho junction. The larger Mucuri drainage farther south is separate.

correspondence.component_scope: Connected middle corridor through Medeiros Neto
correspondence.finding: The selected bends and eastward middle valley follow the repeatedly labeled Rio Alcobaça/Itanhém through Medeiros Neto toward Nova Lídice. The northern Água Fria and Cachoeira do Mato drainage approaches are distinct from the selected trunk. Nearby lagoons south of the river are outside the selected route; the mapped passage is fluvial rather than a selected reservoir crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Nova Lídice to Teixeira de Freitas
correspondence.finding: The Teixeira de Freitas original overlaps Nova Lídice and follows the same river southeast and then east past the northern margin of the city. Its meandering continuation is labeled Alcobaça. The source distinguishes incoming local creeks from the main valley, with no material connector gap at the road crossings or between the adjacent map sheets.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river and actual coastal receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The Alcobaça original follows the lower named Rio Alcobaça through its broad bends into the estuary immediately south of the coastal town and into the Oceano Atlântico. Original terminal pixels distinguish the tidal meanders, coastal spit and sea opening. The retained line simplifies these bends and the coastal approach; it is not treated as a surveyed channel centerline or exact mouth coordinate. The corresponding waterway is the same river estuary, not a different coastal river or inferred distributary.

correspondence.component_scope: Independent regional distinction
correspondence.finding: INEMA’s 2010 map and lower-river sampling network separately identify the Alcobaça corridor between Teixeira de Freitas and Alcobaça, Jucuruçu farther north and Peruípe farther south. Its Alcobaça schematic continues to the ocean. The official committee overview independently places these as distinct constituent basins of the same planning region; the regional grouping is not a single river name.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
